# noust Provider

Manage a [Noust](https://github.com/Perkybeet/noust) server (applications, domains, databases, backups, teams, deploy keys and registry accounts) from Terraform or OpenTofu, through the server's HTTP API.

The provider is a client of the API and implements nothing a server does: every change is the call the console or `noust` would make, behind the same permissions, sudo mode, approvals and audit trail.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    noust = {
      source  = "perkybeet/noust"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

# The address and the token come from NOUST_URL and NOUST_TOKEN, so neither is in the configuration. Use an
# API token made for Terraform (Settings > API tokens in the console, with "Allow sudo mode"), narrowed to
# the permissions of the resources you use: the guide lists them for each one. Never the master token.
provider "noust" {}

# Or, for a server whose certificate comes from a private authority:
#
# provider "noust" {
#   url         = "https://noust.internal.example.com"
#   ca_file     = "/etc/ssl/internal-ca.pem"
#   job_timeout = "45m"
# }
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `approval` (String) The id of an approved request (`X-Noust-Approval`), for a server that asks a second person to approve root-equivalent changes. An approval allows one call, once. Read from `NOUST_APPROVAL` when omitted.
- `ca_file` (String) A PEM file with the certificate authority to trust instead of the system's, for a console on a private certificate. Read from `NOUST_CA_FILE` when omitted. There is no option to skip verification.
- `job_poll_interval` (String) How often to ask the server about a job, as a Go duration. Default `2s`.
- `job_timeout` (String) How long to wait for a job the server queued (a deployment, a removal), as a Go duration such as `30m`. The job keeps running on the server when the wait ends. Default `30m`.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) An API token holding the permissions the configuration needs, issued with `allow_elevated`. Read from `NOUST_TOKEN` when omitted. Never the master token: see the guide for the permissions each resource asks for.
- `url` (String) The console's address, such as `https://noust.example.com`. Read from `NOUST_URL` when omitted. Plain `http://` is accepted only for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1`, because the token would cross the network in clear.
